paragraphs.title: Jehu Is Anointed and the Revolt Begins

easy.explanation: Elisha the prophet sent one of the children of the prophets.
easy.q: Who sent the young prophet to anoint Jehu?

easy.explanation: The prophet took a box of oil and poured it on Jehu's head.
easy.q: What did the prophet pour on Jehu's head?

easy.explanation: They put their garments under him and proclaimed, "Jehu is king."
easy.q: What did the captains proclaim after hearing that Jehu had been anointed?

medium.explanation: He was told to open the door, flee, and not tarry.
medium.q: What was the young prophet told to do after anointing Jehu?

medium.explanation: The expression means to prepare for immediate action and travel.
medium.q: What does "Gird up thy loins" mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: They quickly put their garments under him and blew trumpets.
medium.q: How did the captains respond when Jehu told them about his anointing?

answers: He did not hear the prophet
challenge.explanation: The anointing took place in the inner chamber, and Jehu reported it afterward.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Jehu telling the captains about the anointing only after leaving the room?

challenge.explanation: Jehu was among the captains before being proclaimed king.
challenge.q: What change in Jehu's position is described in these verses?

challenge.explanation: The oil marked Jehu's anointing as king over Israel.
challenge.q: What did the oil signify in this event?

easy.explanation: Jehu conspired against Joram, king of Israel.
Jehu rode in a chariot and went to Jezreel.
easy.q: Toward which city did Jehu travel?

easy.explanation: The watchman saw a company approaching with Jehu.
easy.q: What did the watchman see from the tower?

medium.explanation: Joram and all Israel had kept Ramoth-gilead because of Hazael king of Syria.
medium.q: Why had Joram been keeping Ramoth-gilead?

medium.explanation: The messengers did not return; they followed Jehu.
medium.q: What happened to the messengers sent to Jehu?

medium.explanation: The watchman saw a sizable group approaching.
medium.q: What does "a company" mean in the watchman's report?

challenge.explanation: The watchman said the driving was like the driving of Jehu, who drove furiously.
challenge.q: What helped the watchman identify Jehu's approach?

challenge.explanation: Jehu told each messenger to turn behind him and kept moving forward.
challenge.q: What does Jehu's response to the messengers show about the revolt?

answers: Jehu carried a message of peace
The messengers did not return and the force advanced
challenge.explanation: The messengers failed to return, and Jehu's force continued toward Jezreel.
challenge.q: Why did the watchman's report increase Joram's concern?

paragraphs.title: Jehoram's Death and the Fulfillment of Naboth's Prophecy

easy.explanation: Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out against Jehu.
easy.q: Who went out to meet Jehu?

easy.explanation: They met in the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite.
easy.q: Where did Joram and Jehu meet?

easy.explanation: Jehu drew a bow and struck Jehoram between the arms.
easy.q: What weapon did Jehu use to kill Joram?

answers: Jehu was approaching at the head of a revolt
Jehu had come for a visit
medium.explanation: Jehu's approach with a force caused Joram to question his intentions.
medium.q: Why did Joram ask Jehu, "Is it peace"?

medium.explanation: Jehu connected the lack of peace with Jezebel's whoredoms and witchcrafts.
medium.q: How did Jehu answer Joram's question about peace?

medium.explanation: Jehu referred to Jezebel's wicked conduct as the cause of the trouble.
medium.q: What is meant by "the whoredoms of thy mother Jezebel"?

answers: He died in Naboth's portion, as foretold concerning Naboth's blood
He died in Jerusalem, as foretold concerning Ahaziah
He died at Ramoth-gilead, as foretold concerning Hazael
challenge.explanation: Jehu remembered the LORD's word concerning Naboth's blood and the field.
challenge.q: How was Joram's place of death connected with the prophecy?

challenge.explanation: Jehu told Bidkar to take Joram and cast him into Naboth's portion.
challenge.q: What did Jehu command to be done with Joram's body?

answers: The punishment for Naboth's blood would come upon Ahab's house
challenge.explanation: Jehu applied the LORD's judgment concerning Naboth's blood to Joram.
challenge.q: What connection did Jehu make between Naboth's death and Joram's death?

paragraphs.title: Ahaziah's Death and the Arrival at Jezreel

easy.explanation: Ahaziah fled by the way of the garden house.
easy.q: What did Ahaziah do when he saw what was happening?

easy.explanation: Ahaziah fled to Megiddo and died there.
His servants carried him to Jerusalem and buried him in the city of David.

medium.explanation: He was struck, fled to Megiddo, and died there.
medium.q: What happened to Ahaziah during his flight?

medium.explanation: His servants carried him in a chariot to Jerusalem.
medium.q: Who carried Ahaziah to his burial?

answers: He began to reign in the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab
medium.explanation: The verse gives his accession in relation to Joram's reign.
medium.q: What does the passage state about the time of Ahaziah's reign?

answers: He was buried in the city of David with his fathers
He was buried in Naboth's portion
He was buried where he was wounded
challenge.explanation: The passage says he was carried to Jerusalem and buried in his sepulchre with his fathers.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Ahaziah being buried in Jerusalem although he died at Megiddo?

challenge.explanation: Ahaziah fled, was wounded, and died, so his reign did not continue.
challenge.q: How does the sequence of events affect the kingdom of Judah?

answers: He died near Megiddo and was buried in Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: Megiddo was the place of his death, while Jerusalem was the place of his burial.
challenge.q: What is the main difference between the place where Ahaziah died and where he was buried?

paragraphs.title: Jezebel's Death and the Fulfillment of God's Word

answers: She painted her face and looked out the window
She went out to meet him in the field
easy.explanation: She painted her face, tired her head, and looked out at a window.
easy.q: What did Jezebel do when she heard that Jehu had come to Jezreel?

answers: Throw her down from the window
easy.explanation: Jehu told the eunuchs, "Throw her down."
easy.q: What did Jehu command to be done to Jezebel?

easy.explanation: Dogs ate Jezebel's flesh in the portion of Jezreel.

answers: As Zimri who slew his master
medium.explanation: She said, "Had Zimri peace, who slew his master?"
The eunuchs were attendants in the palace who looked out to Jehu.
medium.q: What does "eunuchs" refer to in this passage?

answers: Her skull, feet, and palms of her hands
medium.explanation: They found no more of her than these remains.
medium.q: What did the people find when they came to bury Jezebel?

answers: Jezebel was buried in the palace
Dogs ate her flesh in the portion of Jezreel
challenge.explanation: The people recognized her fate as the word spoken by the LORD through Elijah.
challenge.q: How was Elijah's prophecy fulfilled at the end of the passage?

answers: The disgrace of her judgment and the fulfillment of God's word
challenge.explanation: The dogs' consumption of her body fulfilled the announced judgment.
challenge.q: What does the absence of a complete body emphasize?

answers: Looking from the window and confronting Jehu
challenge.explanation: She prepared herself, looked out the window, and spoke to Jehu before her death.
challenge.q: What was Jezebel doing before she was thrown from the window?
